notes:
GROUP-SCOPE FINDING (the main ask): confirmed GENUINE, not nominal. list_test_case_tags_v1(project_id=379335744) — the project-scoped sibling — returns exactly the 3 known tags (__mcp-probe-tag-20260918a-renamed, mcp-probe, probe-update; count=3). search_group_tags(entity_type=test_case) for the same group returns 31 distinct test_case tags across 2 pages, the large majority of which (2FA, Booking, Bet, Price, Setup, TOTP, Wallet, admin, android, chrome, backend, cloud, ...) do not belong to project 379335744's 3-tag vocabulary and are clearly drawn from other projects in group 2615. This is the opposite of the pattern found earlier this session with the three user-listing capabilities (where the scope difference was nominal and the same set came back regardless) — here the group listing is a real, different, larger set than the project listing. entity_type=test_run corroborates this further: it returns a completely different-looking vocabulary (commit-hash-like strings, P0, Regression, Java, Python, SQL) consistent with aggregating run tags across many projects, not one.

ENTITY_TYPE ENUM: only 2 declared values (test_case, test_run), both tried, both succeed live with distinct, plausible data — the split is real. A 3rd, undeclared value (test_plan) does NOT reach the backend at all: invokeCapability itself rejects it pre-flight with `'entity_type' must be one of: test_case, test_run` (no http_response, no status code). This directly contradicts describeCapability's guidance text, which explicitly claims entity_type is 'Not validated against a list here... forwarded to the backing service rather than rejected.' The opposite is true — it IS validated, and rejected, before the backend ever sees it. (Unlike the TestPlan-empty-no-error case found elsewhere this session, this is a hard reject, not a silent empty success — but the doc's characterization of the validation behavior is simply wrong.)

ERROR-ENVELOPE DRIFT: describeCapability documents invalid `p` (non-positive/non-numeric) as rejected 'globally with 400 `{success:false, error:"Invalid Params"}`' — implying a backend 400 response. Live: p=0 was rejected as `{"ok":false,"error":"'p' must be at least 1"}` — again no http_response/status at all (invocation-layer rejection, not an API 400), with a different envelope shape (`ok`/string `error` vs documented `success`/object `error`) and a different, more specific message. Never diffed this against the success schema — it has no 2xx counterpart; noting only that the actual rejection shape doesn't match the documented one.

PAGINATION DRIFT: entity_type=test_case, no q — page 1 (p=1): 30 tags, info={page:1,count:31,next:2}. Page 2 (p=2): a further 30 DISTINCT tags (correct continued alphabetical/ASCII sort order, zero overlap with page 1), info={page:2,count:31,next:null}. That is 60 distinct tags actually observed across the two pages, yet both pages report count:31 and page 2 falsely claims next:null as if the vocabulary ended at 31. info.count/next cannot be trusted as an accurate total or end-of-data signal on this endpoint.

MINOR: the known tag `__mcp-probe-tag-20260918a` now returns as `__mcp-probe-tag-20260918a-renamed` — a data change since the task context was written (renamed at some point), not a capability contract issue.

What the docs got RIGHT: this route is the one that resolves tag ids (needed for a tag merge) — confirmed, ids are present and correct-looking on every tag returned. Page size fixed at 30, no per_page param — confirmed. Not permission-gated — consistent with successful calls having no auth-scoping friction beyond the implicit group.
